prd.problem: crates/cna-sim is a deterministic teaching sandbox, not CNA: Unit has HP and percentage fuel/water/ammo, State has one integer stage with STAGE_LIMIT 12 and date_label starting November 1941, move_unit teleports to a reachable endpoint charging cost*8 fuel, attack uses HP damage with sequential retaliation, resupply refills within two hexes of a truck or depot, and end_stage runs an Axis AI and invents periodic hot weather. The complete land, logistics, air, naval, special-rule and scenario systems need section-by-section implementation with evidence, a typed deterministic state model and viewer-safe projections.
prd.why_now: docs/CNAv2.1.0 supplies July 2021 integrated rules (Land 48 pp., Air & Logistics 28 pp., Scenarios 18 pp.; all real PDF content, not LFS pointers, in this worktree), the Sep 79 'incorporated errata.txt', 236 VASSAL chart images keyed by rule case, buildFile.xml and four .vsav setups. These reduce research gaps but expose contradictions: 11.32 prints 'x10' as a 'major correction' while 11.34/11.35 divide by ten (108 raw -> 11 actual); tactical shipping is placed in different phases by 5.2, 33.0 and 48.0; 60.45 narrates one battleship, three cruisers and seven destroyers but its port table lists more; scenario pages 6, 9-10 and 12-16 are image-only; VASSAL v2.1 editorially chose org charts over reinforcement listings and removed first-line trucks from the map. All four saves contain PLAYER records with non-empty password fields. These must be compared and adjudicated before encoding.
prd.users: Players completing official scenarios and the campaign; rules reviewers tracing each decision to sources; map, catalog and movement builders integrating against stable contracts.
prd.value: One simulation orb owns the shared scaffold (workspace members, browser harness, frontend file split, source/credential checks), authoritative state, rules, scenario validation, commands, viewer projections, saves/replay, allowlisted VASSAL import and final gameplay integration. Milestones: (E1) shared scaffold and source baseline, published first so other orbs can start; (E2) command/route/projection contracts with fixtures, a rules coverage ledger, eight adjudication records and a compare leaf for every section 1-65; (E3) deterministic foundation: sandbox isolation, typed state, phase engine for 5/33/48, projection and 3.6 disclosure, saves/replay, import and the abstraction-mode guard; (E4) detailed logistics with maneuver: trucks, supply coordination, fuel/ammo/stores/water, ports/convoys, CPA, initiative, movement, stacking, ZOC, breakdown, weather; (E5) land combat and remaining land sections including raiders, fleet and Rommel; (E6) Graziani's Offensive (section 60.22, 18 OpStages) in land + detailed logistics + section 58 abstract-air mode; (E7) detailed air 33-46 and the alternative abstract modes 32 and 47; (E8) remaining scenarios and the campaign; (E9) final integration and certification gates. Each implemented section has its own issue with a fixtures leaf (expectations hand-derived from the printed rules, examples and charts, written before code and kept ignored until implemented) and one or more implementation leaves; every section also has an E2 compare leaf. Mechanical order differs from printed order; the ledger keeps every section accounted for. Map/catalog contracts feed simulation; simulation publishes route and projection contracts early for movement; simulation correctness never depends on movement animation or catalog UI. Final integration (E9) depends on all three delivered workstreams without creating reverse edges.
success_metrics: data/rules/ledger.json accounts for every numbered case of sections 1-65 found in the July 2021 text (1634 distinct case labels) plus image-only pages; each row links original 1979 rule (physical scan page), identified correction, July 2021 wording, VASSAL chart/save evidence or explicit absence, adjudication id, implementation path and fixture test; `rules-ledger --check` enforces completeness.

VASSAL is treated as a virtual tabletop and bookkeeping source, never an executable rules oracle: every compare leaf lists matching VASSAL charts by case number and records discrepancies rather than copying them.

Eight adjudication records (11.32 strength formula and AA exception; tactical-shipping cadence; 60.45 fleet inventory/release; Cairo vs Cairo/Alexandria supply base; 63.2 duration; errata idempotence and authority classes; abstraction-mode matrix; VASSAL editorial OOB choices) exist before affected implementation; a pending decision blocks certification, not research. Incorporated errata are applied exactly once.

Versioned deterministic commands, events, seeded RNG, save/load and replay preserve Game-Turn/OpStage cadence; rejected commands neither mutate state nor advance RNG. RouteResult carries ordered hexes, per-step CP and fuel, interrupts and reveal events computed from cna-map and cna-catalog data, never frontend-derived rules.

Owner/opponent/observer projections restrict private state across UI, previews, command errors, logs, reports and replay; two states differing only in hidden enemy TOE/cargo produce byte-identical opponent projections until the permitted reveal. L21 3.62 items (stack examination, close assault and anti-armor reveals, patrol, prisoners, broken-down markers, POWs, construction, trucks/RPs, air recon, pilot ratings), dummy tanks/dumps/mines, raiders and secret barrage/force assignments each have a reveal fixture.

Detailed trucks (53), supply coordination (54), fuel (49), ammunition (50), stores (51) and water (52) are implemented in E4 before or with maneuver; weekly and OpStage consumption are distinct, cargo is conserved transactionally and retry/save/reload is idempotent. Abstract sections 32, 47 and 58 are explicit modes enforced by one accounting kernel per resource and never double-charge.

Land 3-31, air 33-46, logistics 48-57, abstractions 32/47/58 and scenarios 59-64 have traceable implementation and verification; sea (30), special rules (27, 31) and Rommel are covered in the Land volume where the rules put them.

Graziani's Offensive (60.22, GT1/1-GT6/3, 18 OpStages) is the first certified scenario, in land + detailed logistics + 58 abstract-air mode, using reviewed map geography and source-linked catalog data; image-only scenario pages are visually transcribed and independently checked before setup certification.

Allowlisted VASSAL import decodes saves in memory, strips PLAYER/password records, reconciles stale GPIDs against the catalog census and writes only a discrepancy report; decoded raw saves are never written or published.

Italian Campaign, Desert Fox (race for Tobruk GT26/3-38/3), Crusader, El Alamein and both campaign starts (to GT111/3) validate OOB, arrivals, withdrawals, resources, victory and special cases; regression traces distinguish sandbox behaviour from certified rules behaviour.

Every leaf is S or M with source sections, boundaries, checkable outputs and real verification commands whose harness is a prerequisite; python3 docs/planning/cna-dag-check.py validates the four-project graph including parent/child completion, cross-project edges, stage order and file ownership.
out_of_scope: Treating an anecdotal play report (docs/story.txt), VASSAL editorial choices or untested abstract rules as superior rules authority.
One enormous implement-the-land-war leaf, or demanding finished terrain or artwork before contracts and rules fixtures can start.
Map tile rendering, sprite production or catalog browsing UI (other orbs).
Online matchmaking, hosted multiplayer or AI opponents; the sandbox Axis AI stays sandbox-only. Viewer boundaries must still prevent leakage.
Claiming full rules fidelity while conflicting or untranscribed requirements remain unresolved.
Changing the existing sandbox's behaviour except to isolate and label it.
open_questions: Graziani's Offensive is proposed as the first certified scenario, followed by the Italian Campaign and the Desert Fox race for Tobruk once their image-only setups are transcribed.
Kevin's decisions are needed for the eight E2.I3 adjudications (research leaves prepare options and a recommendation; work proceeds behind ruleset flags meanwhile).

Global order: E1 scaffold (stage 0) -> producer contracts and comparisons (stage 1) -> foundation and producer deliverables -> mechanics and presentation -> bounded scenario -> remaining systems -> simulation-owned integration. Later producer corrections are new forward leaves with new content versions, never new blockers on completed upstream milestones.

The devkit pipeline schema supports plan-local blocker keys only. Cross-project prerequisites are written in each leaf's scope and machine-listed in docs/planning/cna-dag.manifest.json; Linear relations must be created from that manifest in a second pass and re-read for equality.

subissues.title: Projection engine with redacted previews, errors and logs

subissues.title: L21 3.6 disclosure points
subissues.goal: Reveal exactly what 3.62 allows at the moment it allows it.
scope: Sources: L21 (docs/CNAv2.1.0/Rules_Land_07-2021.pdf) 3.62 pp.6-7

One reveal rule and one fixture per 3.62 item: map stack examination; close assault (participating unit types, not numbers/weapons/losses); anti-armor (tank/SP types, recce/halftrack presence, not numbers/origin/loss allocation); prisoners (nothing beyond the prisoners); patrol (no supplies/attached trucks except motorized); broken-down/destroyed/abandoned markers (contents secret); POWs (numbers and Axis nationality secret); construction item secret; trucks and RPs secret; air recon (less than patrol); planes (makes known in air combat, pilot ratings secret until combat; land units without AA TOE or SGSU learn nothing of bombing/strafing planes).
Mark each case row in the ledger as implemented for 3.6 with its fixture name.
non_goals: Rules that generate the events (later sections call these reveal helpers).
acceptance_criteria: Each fixture shows the opponent projection unchanged before the event and changed by only the allowed fields after it.

subissues.title: Historical replay and export privacy
subissues.goal: Replays show what a viewer knew then, not final-state secrets.
scope: ViewerExport builds from per-viewer knowledge history; replaying to revision r shows the viewer's projection at r; a later reveal never backfills earlier frames.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture: dummy tank revealed at revision 9 appears as unknown in the exported frames 1-8 and as dummy from 9.

issues.title: Product integration
issues.summary: Simulation-owned wiring of all delivered workstreams.

risks: Raw state reaching the UI through an old code path.
acceptance_criteria: Integrated browser acceptance passes.

subissues.title: Official game shell and mode selector
subissues.goal: Let players start an official scenario or the labelled sandbox.

acceptance_criteria: App struct for official games has no field of type GameState (compile-time test); browser test starts Graziani.

subissues.title: Pin map and catalog releases
subissues.goal: Run the product on the released, checksummed producer data.
scope: Cross-project prerequisites (enforced by docs/planning/cna-dag.manifest.json): cna-map:E6.I2.S2 (map-v1.1 release); cna-catalog:E7.I1.S3 (catalog release)
Embed or fetch map-v1.1 and catalog release files by checksum; refuse to start on mismatch; show unresolved counts in an about panel.
acceptance_criteria: Checksum mismatch test; about panel screenshot inspected.

subissues.title: Wire movement playback, inspection and catalog viewer
subissues.goal: Compose the movement and catalog components into the official game.
scope: Cross-project prerequisites (enforced by docs/planning/cna-dag.manifest.json): cna-unit-movement:E5.I1.S2 (movement acceptance); cna-catalog:E7.I1.S2 (catalog browser acceptance)
Mount movement's route playback and inspection with real engine outputs and the catalog browser/modal from the shell; apply any boundary patches the owners supplied.
acceptance_criteria: Browser test: issue a Graziani move, watch per-hex playback, inspect an enemy stack, open the catalog modal.

subissues.title: Local save/load and viewer replay UI
subissues.goal: Let players keep and review games without leaking hidden data.
scope: Save to a local file (download) and load; replay viewer uses ViewerExport history; never offers the opponent's private save.
acceptance_criteria: Browser test saves, reloads and replays; exported file passes the sentinel scan.

subissues.title: End-to-end browser acceptance and privacy scan
subissues.goal: Prove the integrated product on the real stack.
scope: Play GT1/OpStage1 of Graziani through the UI for both sides (hot-seat with viewer switch), capture screenshots at 2458x1358 and 1280x800, rerun the sentinel privacy scan over DOM, titles, ARIA, logs and exported replay.
acceptance_criteria: Screenshots inspected; zero sentinel leaks; console clean.

acceptance_criteria: Gates run and report.

subissues.title: Full product certification gate
subissues.goal: Combine rules, geography, unit data and unique-art coverage into one honest statement.

acceptance_criteria: Report generated; overall status 'certified' only with zero blockers.
